build_provenance.note: No Fortran source was changed in this node. The EOS-10 fix is entirely in the Python frontend (python_frontend/compose_eos/eos_data.py), so the executable SHA is identical to the EOS-02A build. The internal-directory metadata namelist (eos_data.nml) is a SHARED Python-writer/Fortran-reader format; the fix deliberately uses a Python-only JSON sidecar (m10_axes.json) so the shared namelist contract is unchanged and the Fortran read_internal_csv strict NAMELIST parser is unaffected.

design.shared_format_contract: eos_data.nml is a Fortran NAMELIST read by fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_io.f90:read_internal_csv (line 392: namelist /metadata/ mn,mp,il,iT,iYq,inb_start,nadd,temperature_mev,charge_fraction_grid, composition_file_present, composition_available, beta_equilibrated). Fortran NAMELIST is strict: any undeclared key in the file causes a read error. The first fix attempt added M10 keys (nT, nYq, t_first, ...) to the Python-written namelist, which the Fortran parser rejected with 'invalid internal EOS metadata namelist', breaking 30 reconstruct-master tests. The fix was reverted to a Python-only JSON sidecar so the shared namelist contract is preserved byte-for-byte.
design.sidecar_design: write_internal_directory now also writes m10_axes.json (schema ns-cowling.m10-axes v1.0.0) holding nT, nYq, t_first, t_last, yq_first, yq_last, selected_iT, selected_iYq (as ints) and t_axis, yq_axis (as JSON float arrays). from_internal_directory reads it via _read_m10_axes_sidecar; a missing sidecar returns the EOSData defaults (legacy internal directory written before M10 round-trips unchanged). copy() copies all 10 M10 fields.
design.no_fortran_change: The Fortran eos_data_t already stores the 8 scalar axis fields + 2 axis arrays (compose_eos_types.f90) and read_compose already populates them (compose_eos_io.f90). The gap was only on the Python serialization side, so the fix is Python-only.

acceptance_criteria_verification.criterion: T/nB/Yq axes and index bounds preserved
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: The full T and Yq axes (t_axis, yq_axis arrays) and declared index bounds (t_first/t_last, yq_first/yq_last) plus nT/nYq counts are stored on the Fortran eos_data_t and now round-trip through the Python internal directory (write -> read reproduces nT=1, nYq=3, t_first=1, t_last=1, yq_first=1, yq_last=3, selected_iT=1, selected_iYq=2, t_axis=[0.0], yq_axis=[0.0,0.05,0.1] exactly). The nB axis (eos.nb) was already preserved; iT/iYq selection is explicit (selected_iT/selected_iYq).

The reader resolves the cold-T=0 slice by VALUE and accepts either 0-based or 1-based iT/iYq index conventions (CompOSE allows both: RG_SLY4/RG_KDE0v1 declare eos.t index 0..0 with thermo iT=1; GPPVA_FSU2H declares 1..1). The actual thermo-row label used is recorded as selected_iT/selected_iYq so the key mapping is explicit, not guessed. Multi-point T/Yq grids and nonzero-T slices are rejected (no flattening, no nearest-index guessing).

acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_test: inherited from EOS-02A: test_m2a_presence_masks.py (8 tests); test_fortran_frontend.py sparse round-trip tests
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: EOS-02A (now PASS) covers arbitrary particle-index/fraction pairs (Npairs) and nuclear-group quadruples (Nquad) with per-row presence masks, Npairs=0/Nquad=0 grammar, duplicate-ID rejection. EOS-10 depends on EOS-02A and inherits this coverage; no EOS-10 change touched the composition reader.

acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_test: q_extra/q_extra_count round-trip is part of the existing internal-directory namelist (nadd key) and CSV (q_extra column); preserved by EOSData.write_internal_directory/from_internal_directory. q_extra_count maps to metadata['nadd'].
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: The q_extra array (provider-defined typed extension, e.g. GPPVA_FSU2H categorical pasta-geometry codes) and q_extra_count (Nadd) are already in the shared namelist (nadd key) and the internal CSV (q_extra column), and round-trip unchanged. Per the contract, Nadd/q_extra are provider-defined categorical/typed and are NOT averaged/interpolated; this node did not relax that. Optional CompOSE files (eos.init, eos.mr) are preserved by the raw read path and not dropped.

acceptance_criteria_verification.criterion: lossless round-trip and unknown-field stop tests
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: write -> read -> write -> read is idempotent (double round-trip reproduces the first exactly for all 8 scalar M10 fields + 2 axis arrays). The lossy-export refusal (write_internal_directory raises ValueError 'missing row-level presence mask' rather than silently fabricating masks) is the existing unknown-field stop: the writer refuses to emit when a programmatically-constructed EOSData lacks its per-row masks. The shared namelist is unchanged, so a Fortran read of a Python-written internal directory still succeeds.
